header_desc_1: DarkMoon Engine is a custom graphics engine developed from scratch in C++23 and OpenGL. It was originally created to support Two Wonders, focusing on meeting the project's technical and graphical requirements while handling complex scenes efficiently.
header_desc_2: This new version of the engine focuses exclusively on 2D, providing a more stable and modular architecture compared to the previous iteration. It includes a refactor of the original codebase, reorganizing systems to improve clarity, scalability, and maintainability.
header_ecs: Entity Component System built on top of a custom SlotMap and compile-time type metaprogramming. Header-only, zero dynamic allocation, designed to be instantiated by the user with their own component and tag types.
whatis_desc: Entity Component System is an architectural pattern that separates data (components) from logic (systems), using lightweight handles (entities) to group them.
whatis_core_entity: Entity: a numeric ID with a bitmask of which components and tags it owns. No data of its own.
whatis_core_component: Component: a plain data struct (e.g. PhysicsComponent, RenderComponent). No logic.
whatis_core_tag: Tag: an empty struct used as a boolean flag on an entity (e.g. TagPlayer, TagEnemy). Zero memory cost in the SlotMap.
whatis_core_system: System: a struct with an update(EM&, ...) method that iterates entities and acts on their components.
whatis_core_em: Entity Manager: owns all entities and component storage. Instantiated by the user with their concrete types.
whatis_design_headeronly: Fully header-only, all code lives in .hpp files because it is 100% template-based.
whatis_design_slotmap: Component storage uses a SlotMap per component type for O(1) access and cache-friendly iteration.
whatis_design_bitmask: Bitmasks are computed at compile time via MP::cmp_tag_traits, no runtime type lookup.
whatis_design_limits: Maximum 200 entities and 350 slots per SlotMap by default, change via template parameters.
whatis_design_types: The user defines their own CMPList and TAGList in types.hpp. The engine provides no predefined components.
architecture_desc: DarkMoon uses a compile-time ECS where component and tag lists are defined by the user, keeping the engine fully type-safe and zero-overhead.
architecture_dataflow_desc: The user instantiates an EntityManager via types.hpp and interacts with entities through a clean API creating, adding components, querying, and iterating with lambdas.
typeshpp_desc: types.hpp is the single file you edit when adding new components or tags to your game. It instantiates the EntityManager with your concrete types.
architecture_types_reminder: Remember to add every new component or tag to CMPList / TAGList in types.hpp, or the EntityManager won't know they exist.
components_desc: Components are plain data structs. They contain no logic.
components_list_1: Components must be default-constructible (required by the SlotMap).
components_list_2: Keep components small and focused, one responsibility per struct.
components_list_3: Components can own heap data via std::unique_ptr but be aware of move semantics when the SlotMap reorganizes storage.
tags_desc: Tags are empty structs used as boolean flags on entities. They cost only a single bit in the entity's bitmask, no SlotMap storage is allocated.
systems_desc: Systems are structs with an update() method. They receive the EM by reference and use forEach to iterate entities that match their required components and tags.
systems_callout: Systems should declare SYSCMPs and SYSTAGs as type aliases inside the struct. It makes the system self-documenting and allows other systems or debug tools to inspect requirements at compile time.
api_newEntity: Creates a new entity and returns a reference to it. Asserts if MAX_ENTITIES (200) is reached.
api_destroyEntityByID: Finds the entity with the given ID and destroys it along with all its components. Uses swap-with-last internally for O(1) removal.
api_destroyEntities: Batch-destroys a set of entity indices. The set must be sorted in descending order (std::greater) to avoid index invalidation during removal.
api_destroyAll: Destroys all alive entities and resets all component storages.
api_getEntityByID: Returns a pointer to the entity with the given ID, or nullptr if not found. Linear search — avoid calling every frame.
api_getEntities: Returns a span over all currently alive entities. Safe to iterate while not destroying entities.
api_aliveCount: Returns the number of currently alive entities.
api_freeEntities: Returns how many more entities can be created before hitting MAX_ENTITIES.
api_entity_getID: Returns the unique ID of this entity. IDs are assigned sequentially and never reused within a session.
api_entity_hasComponent: Returns true if the entity currently owns a component of type T. Checked via bitmask: O(1).
api_entity_hasTag: Returns true if the entity has the given tag. Checked via bitmask: O(1).
